CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  2175 Cherry Avenue • Signal Hill, California 90755-3799

  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  WELCOMES YOU TO A REGULAR
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  July 25, 2023

Meetings begin at 6:00 pm with the conduct of any business permitted to be conducted in
closed session by the Brown Act (Government Code Section 54950, et seq.), if any, and with
the public portion of the meeting beginning at 7:00 pm. There is a period for public comment
on closed session matters at 6:00 pm prior to the closed session. In the event there is no
business to be conducted in closed session, the regular meeting shall begin at 7:00 pm.
There is a public comment period at the beginning of the regular meeting. Any person
wishing to comment shall be allotted three minutes per distinct item. Any meeting may be
adjourned to a time and place stated in the order of adjournment.

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting on the City’s website and outside of City
Hall. The agenda and related reports are also available for review online at
www.cityofsignalhill.org.

This meeting will be held in person and via teleconference pursuant to Government Code
Sections 54953(b) and 54953(c) at the Council Chambers of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue,
Signal Hill, CA 90755 and 42 Baka Road, Madison, ME 04950.

To view or listen to the meeting live at 7:00 p.m.:

  •  City of Signal Hill website at www.cityofsignalhill.org, select the City Council
  Meetings Link from the home page.
  •  Charter Spectrum Channel 3 or Frontier FiOS Channel 38.
  •  Call (408) 638-0968 (audio only) and enter meeting ID: 881-4793-6648, press #
  when prompted to provide participant ID, and enter passcode: 374778. If you would
  like to make a public comment, please notify the meeting host by pressing *9 on the
  telephone keypad.
To view and participate (closed session at 6:00 p.m. and regular meeting at 7:00 p.m.):

  • In-person Participation: Council Chambers of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal
  Hill, CA 90755 and 42 Baka Road, Madison, ME 04950.
  • Remote Participation: Visit https://zoom.us/j/88147936648 on your desktop
  computer or laptop and enter passcode: 374778; or

  Page 1 of 8
 City Council  Regular  July 25, 2023

  • Visit www.zoom.us on your desktop computer or laptop, click on “Join a Meeting”,
  and enter meeting ID: 881-4793-6648 and passcode: 374778 when prompted; or
  • Download the app from the app store if you are using a smart phone and enter
  meeting ID: 881-4793-6648 and passcode: 374778 when prompted.
  • Please note that you will be placed in a “listen only” mode and your video feed will
  not be shared with the Council or public. If you would like to make a public comment,
  please notify the meeting host by raising your virtual hand (see hand icon at bottom of
  screen) and you will be invited to speak when the City Council is taking public
  comments. Please do not simultaneously use a microphone through Zoom and a
  cellphone/telephone. That combination results in audio problems for all participants.
  • To make a general public comment or comment on a specific agenda item, you may
  also submit your comment, limited to 250 words or less, to the City Clerk at
  cityclerk@cityofsignalhill.org not later than 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, July 25, 2023.
  Written comments will be provided electronically to City Council and attached to the
  meeting minutes. Written comments will not be read into the record.
  • Please note that remote participation is offered as a public service and the City is
  not responsible for meeting disruptions or technical difficulties; however, if you are
  disconnected, please repeat the steps above. Submission of written comments or
  in-person participation will ensure that your comments are received.
City Council Members are compensated $722.18 per month. City Clerk and City Treasurer are
compensated $438.22 per month.

  a.  THE PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT WILL PROVIDE A PRESENTATION

  b.  THE CITY OF LONG BEACH ANIMAL CARE SERVICES DEPARTMENT WILL

  c.  REPRESENTATIVES FROM THE CHILDREN’S CLINIC WILL PROVIDE AN
  OVERVIEW AND UPDATES REGARDING THE SERVICES THE
  ORGANIZATION PROVIDES TO SIGNAL HILL RESIDENTS.

(12)  PUBLIC HEARING

  a.  PUBLIC HEARING - CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 23-01 TO OPERATE THE
  LONG BEACH FIREFIGHTERS’ ASSOCIATION CORPORATION LOCAL 372
  AS DEFINED BY THE SIGNAL HILL MUNICIPAL CODE AND TO ALLOW
  LIMITED LARGE EVENTS AND USE OF THE ADJACENT CITY PARKING LOT
  PURSUANT TO AN EXECUTED LICENSE AGREEMENT AND FINDING THAT
  SAID ACTION IS CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA) PURSUANT TO STATE CEQA
  GUIDELINES SECTION 15301

  Summary:

  Form of Notice: Notice was published in the Signal Tribune newspaper per
  Government Code §65091(a)(4) on July 14, 2023; mailed to property owners
  and residents within a 300’ radius of the subject site on July 14, 2023; mailed to
  property owners and residents on North Legion Drive and on the north side of
  East Hill Street between North Legion Drive and Rose Avenue on July 14, 2023;
  and posted in accordance with Signal Hill Municipal Code (SHMC) Section
  1.08.010 at City Hall, Signal Hill Library, Reservoir Park, and Discovery Well
  Park on July 14, 2023.

  Kevin Scott, the authorized agent on behalf of the property owner, the Long
  Beach Firefighters’ Association Corporation Local 372 (LBFFA), is requesting a
  Page 3 of 8
 City Council  Regular  July 25, 2023

  Conditional Use Permit to operate a club as defined by SHMC Section
  20.04.153, to include holding events at its existing offices at 2201 Cherry
  Avenue as allowed in the Commercial Residential (CR) zoning district.
  Recommendations:

  1. Adopt a resolution approving Conditional Use Permit 23-01, to allow
  operation of a club with associated, limited large events, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 23-01, A
  REQUEST TO OPERATE A CLUB, AS DEFINED BY THE SIGNAL HILL
  MUNICIPAL CODE, AND TO ALLOW A LIMITED NUMBER OF LARGE
  EVENTS AND THE USE OF THE ADJACENT CITY PARKING LOT
  PURSUANT TO AN EXECUTED LICENSE AGREEMENT AT 2201
  CHERRY AVENUE IN THE COMMERCIAL RESIDENTIAL (CR) ZONING
  DISTRICT AND FINDING THAT SAID ACTION IS CATEGORICALLY
  EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT
  (CEQA) PURSUANT TO STATE CEQA GUIDELINES SECTION 15301

  2. Adopt a resolution approving the Parking License Agreement between the
  City of Signal Hill and the LBFFA, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE A
  PARKING LICENSE AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  AND THE LONG BEACH FIREFIGHTERS’ ASSOCIATION ALLOWING
  NON-EXCLUSIVE, LIMITED, AND CONDITIONAL USE OF THE CITY
  PARKING LOTS AT 1919 EAST HILL STREET AND FINDING THAT SAID
  ACTION IS CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA) PURSUANT TO STATE CEQA
  GUIDELINES SECTION 15301
(13)  CITY MANAGER REPORTS

  a.  CONTRACT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH JOHN KALISKI ARCHITECTS,
  INC. FOR CIVIC CENTER MASTER PLAN SERVICES

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider approving a Contract Services Agreement with
  John Kaliski Architects, Incorporated (JKA) for preparation of a Civic Center
  Master Plan, in the amount of $218,915 with a contingency of $31,085. The City
  released a Request for Proposals (RFP) for these services on May 5, 2023, with
  a proposal due date of June 15, 2023; the City received eight proposals by the
  deadline. Following staff review of proposals and interviews, JKA was the
  highest ranked firm. Based on the evaluation process, staff believes JKA is the
  best qualified firm to work with community stakeholders to prepare a
  comprehensive redesign of the Civic Center campus, develop conceptual site

  Page 4 of 8
 City Council  Regular  July 25, 2023

  plans based on feedback, and identify a funding plan for each option. If
  approved by City Council, JKA believes the work can be completed within a
  five-month period from the contract start date.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a Contract Services Agreement with
  John Kaliski Architects Incorporated for preparation of a Civic Center Master
  Plan, in the amount of $218,915, in a form approved by the City Attorney;
  and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve a contingency in the amount not to
  exceed $31,085 to match the City Council’s appropriation of $250,000.
  b.  CONSIDERATION OF ATTENDANCE CALENDAR

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider the process to report an absence prior to a City
  Council meeting and consider establishing a City Council attendance calendar.
  Recommendation:

  Provide direction to staff.
(14)  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following Consent Calendar items are expected to be routine and
  non-controversial. Items will be acted upon by the Council at one time without
  discussion. Any item may be removed by a Council Member for discussion.
  a.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT REGISTER DATED JULY 25, 2023

  Summary:

  The Contract Amendment Register is a listing of proposed contract amendments
  and project change orders eligible for streamlined processing based upon the
  following criteria as documented in the City’s Purchasing Policy:

  ·  Funds have been authorized as part of the adopted fiscal year Operating
  Budget.
  ·  Staff are satisfied with the goods/services received to date; and
  ·  City Manager reviewed and approved each amendment for streamlined
  processing.

  The contract amendments being presented for City Council consideration are as
  follows:

  FCG Consultants, Incorporated: Services for Spring Street Bicycle Lane Gap
  Closure project (90.18003). Amendment No. 2 extends the term by nine months
  through September 30, 2023, and increases the compensation by $41,019.56

  Page 5 of 8
 City Council  Regular  July 25, 2023

  due to project delays and additional services. The revised total not-to-exceed
  contract amount is $322,712.56.

  Tetra Tech, Incorporated: Services for Well 10 Construction project (95.18011).
  Amendment No. 2 extends the term by 5 months through November 30, 2023,
  and increases the total compensation by $17,000 to a new not-to-exceed
  contract amount of $475,000 for additional services for permit information.

  Architerra Incorporated dba Architerra Design Group: Professional design
  services for Hillbrook Park Renovation Design project (80.23007). Amendment
  No. 1 extends the term by 8 months through March 30, 2024, due to scheduling
  delays and to provide additional support services.

  SWA Group, Incorporated: Professional architectural design services for the
  Citywide Median Landscape project (90.23006). Amendment No. 1 extends the
  term by 10 months through May 30, 2024, due to scheduling delays and provide
  additional support services; the amendment does not provide additional
  compensation.
  Recommendation:

  Authorize the Contract Amendment Register dated July 25, 2023.
  b.  RESOLUTION AMENDING THE CONFLICT OF INTEREST CODE

  Summary:

  Government Code Section 87300 et. seq. requires local governments review
  their respective conflict of interest code to determine its accuracy or make
  amendments as necessary. Currently, staff believes it is necessary to amend
  the City’s Conflict of Interest Code to update the list of designated employees to
  ensure consistency with the recently updated City Council-approved Personnel
  Summary.
  Recommendation:

  Adopt the resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING RESOLUTION NO. 2021-09-6640, AMENDING THE
  CONFLICT OF INTEREST CODE FOR THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  c.  RESOLUTION DESIGNATING AUTHORIZED AGENTS OF THE CITY OF
  SIGNAL HILL FOR CALIFORNIA’S OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES
  PUBLIC ASSISTANCE GRANTS

  Summary:

  The City of Signal Hill declared a local emergency in accordance with California
  Government Code 8630 and the Signal Hill Municipal Code in response to the

  Page 6 of 8
 City Council  Regular  July 25, 2023

  COVID-19 pandemic. Staff submitted an application requesting reimbursement
  for expenses related to the COVID-19 pandemic to the Federal Emergency
  Management Agency and the California Governor’s Office of Emergency
  Services (Cal OES). Cal OES is requesting the City complete the Request for
  Public Assistance Application and Cal OES Form 130.
  Recommendation:

  Adopt the following resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, DESIGNATING THE CITY MANAGER, THE CHIEF OF POLICE,
  AND THE DEPUTY CITY MANAGER AS AUTHORIZED AGENTS TO
  EXECUTE APPLICATIONS ON BEHALF OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL FOR
  THE PURPOSE OF OBTAINING POST-DISASTER ASSISTANCE GRANTS
  FROM CALIFORNIA GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES
  AND FEDERAL EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AGENCY
  d.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS AND MONTHLY TRANSACTION REPORT

  Summary:

  The Schedule of Investments is a listing of all surplus funds invested for both the
  City and the Successor Agency to the former Signal Hill Redevelopment Agency
  as of the date shown on the report. The monthly transaction report provides the
  changes in investments for the prior month.
  Recommendation:

  Receive and file.
  e.  WARRANT REGISTER DATED JULY 25, 2023

  Summary:

  The Warrant Register is a listing of all general disbursements issued since the
  prior warrant register and warrants to be released upon City Council approval.
  Recommendation:

  Authorize payment of the Warrant Register dated July 25, 2023.
  f.  APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES

  Summary:

  Regular Meeting of July 11, 2023.
  Recommendation:

  Approve the meeting minutes.

(16)  ADJOURNMENT

  Tonight’s meeting will be adjourned to the next regular meeting of the Signal Hill City
  Council to be held on Tuesday, August 8, 2023, at 7:00 p.m. (hybrid meeting format,
  including in-person, and video and teleconference participation options). Instructions to
  participate in the meeting will be provided on the meeting agenda.
CITIZEN PARTICIPATION

  Routine matters are handled most quickly and efficiently if contact is made with the City
  department directly concerned. However, if you would like to request that a matter be
  presented for City Council consideration, you may do so by writing to the City Council,
  City Clerk, or City Manager. The deadline for agenda items is 12 noon on the Tuesday
  preceding the Council and Agency meetings. The complete agenda, including back up
  materials is available on the City website on the Friday preceding the meeting.

  If you need special assistance beyond what is normally provided to participate in City
  meetings, the City will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner.
  Please call the City Clerk's office at (562) 989-7305 at least 48 hours prior to the
  meeting to inform us of your particular needs and to determine if accommodation is
  feasible.
